this_run_closures.lesson: The hunter call worked and I am discounting it anyway, because the post-mortem found a better explanation than the one I wrote. I predicted the 1.25x switch threshold would hand hunter a rotation near the lows, and it did rotate twice. But BOTH of the session's worst entries across the whole fleet - hunter's UPRO at 146.60 and hype's CRWV at 85.61 - were stamped at the same instant, 15:45:46Z, the first cycle after a 6-hour blackout, and both landed within 1% of their day's high. That is not eight bots independently chasing extremes; that is one broken scheduler handing every bot a single late-session print. My re-entry thesis has been scoring the symptom. It stays open one more cycle only because it is now stated in a form that can distinguish the two - see 2026-08-04-hunter-1.

fill_integrity.logic_defect_found: NOT a fill-integrity alert - both prices verify - but a genuine defect worth the owner's attention. In commit 0246d462 hunter executed SELL USO 120.18 on a trailing stop and BUY USO 120.18 in the SAME cycle at the IDENTICAL price. Net P/L zero, but it reset the high-water mark from ~130.65 to 120.18, which disarmed the stop that had just fired. A trailing stop whose selection engine can immediately re-buy the asset it just stopped out of is not a stop; it is a high-water-mark reset with extra steps. Reported only - I do not modify bot code.

stalled_bots.why_it_is_a_different_fault: The 2026-08-03 staleness check exists to catch ONE bot going stale against a healthy fleet - a freeze-guard misfire. Here the age is 407 min for all nine with a 13-second spread, which is the signature of the loop process ending, not of any guard. Job 30859366503, queued from 22:37:40Z, was cancelled at 07:26:20Z without ever running. GitHub then accepted no scheduled start until 08:08:28Z (job 30890697953, now in_progress), so the fleet was dark from the last cycle commit at 01:17:54Z until 08:08:28Z.

operational_flag.escalation_evidence: THIS IS THE RUN THAT MAKES THE COST CONCRETE, and it is the strongest argument for the external trigger the owner has already pre-agreed to. The 360-minute gap did not fall at night - it ran 09:46-15:45 ET, the middle six hours of the highest-dispersion session in the sample. Consequences that are visible in the fills rather than inferred: (1) hunter sold USO at 09:46 ET and could not act again until 15:45 ET, when it bought UPRO at 146.60, within 0.18% of the day's high; (2) hype bought CRWV at 85.61 in the same 15:45:46Z cycle, within 0.68% of ITS day's high; (3) the Analyst made its single decision at 09:32 ET and had no cycle in which to revisit it all session; (4) crypto ran no cycle while BTC moved 63,017 -> 63,901. Three of the fleet's four worst entry prices this session share one timestamp - 15:45:46Z - and that timestamp is the moment the infrastructure came back, not a moment any strategy chose. A blackout that ends late in a strong up-day systematically buys the high. The gaps are no longer just an availability metric; they are a source of measurable negative selection in the fills.
operational_flag.pattern: Gap duration is still in the same tight band - 360 and 407 min against 357-376 across the prior four - so the mechanism is unchanged: bot.yml runs a ~5h45m self-looping job under concurrency group 'bot' with cancel-in-progress:false, and GitHub accepts roughly 6% of the 72 requested cron starts per day. When a job ends, the fleet is dark until GitHub happens to accept another start. What HAS changed is the phase: the gaps have drifted off the night window the escalation was originally scoped to and now land in market hours.
operational_flag.failed_runs: No FAILED runs in the last 30. Of the last 5 paper-trade-cycle runs, 2 read 'cancelled' (30859366503, 30795844538) - both consistent with the concurrency-lock mechanism, not with bot errors.
